description:
Free. The upload fee is charged by confirm_datasheet_upload, after the file is checked. Gives a signed URL to upload a datasheet PDF we don't have: use it when datasheet_status is 'no_source' (once the search has finished: not while it is 'resolving') or 'unsupported'. Three steps:
1. Call this with the MPN, the file's SHA-256 and its byte size; you get upload_url, upload_method ('PUT'), upload_headers and an upload_token.
2. Upload the bytes: `curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/pdf' --data-binary @file.pdf "$UPLOAD_URL"` (plus any upload_headers).
3. Call confirm_datasheet_upload with the upload_token.
Checked at confirm (nothing charged if a check fails): a parseable PDF, the SHA-256 and size you declared, and the MPN or its stem on the first page (scanned image-only PDFs fail this). Max 50 MB; the part's datasheet, not a dev-kit manual, schematic or app note. Uploaded datasheets are private to your organisation. Tokens expire after 15 minutes; request a new one if needed.

expected_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the PDF bytes (64 chars), e.g. from `shasum -a 256 file.pdf`.

manufacturer.description: Optional manufacturer name (e.g. 'Texas Instruments') when the MPN alone is ambiguous.

part_number.description: MPN the PDF belongs to. Not a value or description.

size_bytes.description: Size of the PDF in bytes (1,024 to 50,000,000).

name: request_datasheet_upload
title: Request Datasheet Upload
